args.body:
Hello,

We have three open lines with you for the battery pack, 48 V 30 Ah LFP (HR-50110): HPO-26-00429/20 (227 EA, promised 28 September), HPO-26-00560/10 (229 EA, promised 21 October) and HPO-26-00609/10 (179 EA, promised 19 November).

Please send us, as soon as you can and no later than 15 October:

1. A certificate of origin or other proof of origin for HR-50110, showing the country where the pack is made.
2. The tariff (HTS) classification you use for HR-50110.
3. The planned ship date for HPO-26-00609/10, which is currently promised for 19 November.

Please also confirm the current ship status of HPO-26-00429/20 and HPO-26-00560/10.

This is a request for information only and does not change any order or commit Halden to anything.

Thank you,
Halden Robotics Procurement

recommendation.finding:
The new 25% duty from 1 November hits the 48 V 30 Ah battery pack, which is China-origin: $501K is owed, with $862K gross beside it. Halden is importer of record on all three open Quenvara lines. The 28 September and 21 October lines enter in time. The 19 November line (HPO-26-00609/10) carries $51K more, owed only if it ships after 1 November, and no record holds its ship date. The 1,763 units with no open order fall at the full 25%. A request to Quenvara's contact on file (Wang Fang) for proof of origin, the tariff code and that ship date is drafted and waits for approval. Nothing is sent. Priya Nair also has a logged question on freight, the blank Incoterm and the broker's origin ruling. Act by 15 October.

The other source is not cheaper on what is known. Quenvara's Shenzhen quote QV-Q-2609-17 lands at $1,444.01 against $1,421.40 last paid. It is China (Huizhou) origin, 45 days from order, Incoterm Shenzhen, valid to 5 November. Quenvara's Penang quote claims Malaysia origin, available only from 1 February 2027 after site qualification. That origin is to confirm. If ruled China it lands at $1,530.65.
